page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 400 GB SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with high scores in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded text processing and compression tasks. However, multi-core performance, including multi-threaded decompression and software compilation, falls into the average tier. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff: while read bandwidth is average, large-block write bandwidth and overall PassMark memory scores are positioned in the lower tier.

Given its high memory density relative to the 8 shared vCPUs, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources or sustained multi-core compute. It is well-suited for large-scale caching, in-memory databases, text processing, and web serving. However, it is less optimal for heavy multi-threaded workloads or medium-to-large language model inference due to its shared CPU allocation and weaker memory write speeds.
